job.style: a market or shop situation that uses the idea

passage: Rohan is helping his father manage a triangular plot of land near the local market to set up a vegetable stall. The plot has sides measuring 12 meters, 16 meters, and 20 meters. To calculate the area for planning the layout, Rohan first converts all measurements into meters, ensuring he does not mix units like centimeters with meters. He knows that the height of a triangle is not necessarily one of its sides, so he avoids assuming the slanting side is the altitude. Instead, he calculates the semi-perimeter by adding the three sides and dividing by two, which gives him 24 meters. He then uses Heron’s formula, taking the square root of the product of the semi-perimeter and the differences between the semi-perimeter and each side. Rohan realizes that a quadrilateral plot nearby with sides of 5, 6, 7, and 8 meters cannot be solved using Heron’s formula directly because the formula is specifically for triangles. He decides to split that quadrilateral into two triangles by drawing a diagonal. Finally, he remembers that the area of a triangle is always half the product of the base and height, but since he lacks the height, Heron’s formula is the perfect tool to find the area without needing to measure the altitude first.

items.evidence: To calculate the area for planning the layout, Rohan first converts all measurements into meters, ensuring he does not mix units like centimeters with meters.
items.q: One side of a plot is in centimetres, two are in metres. What should Rohan do before using Heron's formula?
options: Write every side in metres first
Write every side just as it is given
Write only the longest side in metres
Write every side in metres after finding area
items.explain: Rohan converts all sides to metres before calculating, so units are never mixed in the formula.

wrong.why: thinks m and cm can go into the formula as they are
thinks only the biggest number needs changing
thinks units can be fixed at the end

items.evidence: He knows that the height of a triangle is not necessarily one of its sides, so he avoids assuming the slanting side is the altitude.
items.q: Meena takes a slanting side of a triangle as its height. Why is this a mistake?
options: Height may not lie along any side
Height should be the base side instead
Height should be the longest side instead
Height is never needed for any triangle
items.explain: A triangle's height is not necessarily one of its sides, so a slanting side cannot be assumed as altitude.

wrong.why: thinks the height is always one of the sides
thinks height can be measured along some slanting side
misreads Heron's formula as meaning height never matters

items.evidence: Instead, he calculates the semi-perimeter by adding the three sides and dividing by two, which gives him 24 meters.

options: Half of the plot's total boundary length
The plot's full total boundary length

items.explain: 24 m is the semi-perimeter: the three sides added (48 m) and divided by two.
